label: Heavy weather
summary: The world edges up a point to 35, still firmly in the 'Bad' band, as a first flicker of Gulf diplomacy is set against a continent on fire and a river valley under water. The US bombed Iran for a 13th consecutive night, a missile strike on Ahvaz killing four people and injuring five, while the Pentagon quietly revised its own war death toll down from 18 to 14 on the argument that some deaths followed President Trump's April ceasefire declaration; the House passed another War Powers Resolution 214-208 with four Republicans in favour, though the Senate rejected a companion measure 47-49. The day's genuine opening came through Islamabad: Reuters reported that Pakistan and Iran are exploring a path back to talks with Washington in a push initiated by China, with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni making his second visit to Pakistan in ten days and meeting army chief Asim Munir, and Beijing saying it supports the mediation. Oil fell for the first time in a week, Brent dropping almost 4 percent to settle at 96.78 dollars after touching 102, and Wall Street steadied, the S&P 500 up 3.68 points to 7,411.98 and the Dow up 0.5 percent even as the Nasdaq slid 0.6 percent and all three indexes closed the week lower. Against that, Europe's fire season turned severe: Spain declared a national emergency with about 10,000 evacuated around Madrid and nine further serious fires burning, 1,140 square kilometres already scorched this year, more than five times the same period in 2025, while France evacuated over 60,000 people from Gironde and the Landes, some by boat, and both countries called in EU firefighting aircraft from Croatia, Portugal, Czechia, Slovakia, Italy and Greece as Almeria was forecast to hit 44C. In India's Assam, Brahmaputra flooding killed at least 50 people and displaced 700,000, submerging nearly 900 villages. Trump's new tariffs of 10 to 12.5 percent on the EU, Canada, Mexico, India, China, Japan and South Korea took effect, the FAO warned that Hormuz disruption could stall progress against a hunger burden already touching 645 million people, and diesel up more than 60 percent year on year has cost US farmers an extra 1.4 billion dollars. Guyana's ferry disaster toll reached 65 of 133 aboard the MV Barima. The brighter column was modest but real: a Brazilian ex-Navy commander drew 24 years for plotting a coup, Argentina won a 250-million-dollar CAF guarantee, the Pacific De-Risking Group met at the Forum Secretariat as the region marked a year since the ICJ climate ruling, and astronomers confirmed the first atmosphere ever detected around a rocky planet in another star's habitable zone. The headline matches the rubric formula with no adjustment.

drivers.headline: US Central Command bombs Iran for a 13th consecutive night, with a missile strike on Ahvaz killing four people and injuring five as strikes hit multiple cities; the Pentagon revises the American death toll in the war down from 18 to 14, arguing some fatalities occurred after President Trump's April ceasefire declaration, while the House approves another War Powers Resolution 214-208 calling for the withdrawal of US forces from hostilities against Iran with four Republicans in support, a measure the Senate then rejects 47-49

Four Palestinians and one Israeli are killed when dozens of settlers attack the town of Tal, west of Nablus in the occupied West Bank; 86 Palestinians have now been killed in the West Bank since the start of 2026, more than 20 of them shot by settlers, in a pattern of violence running alongside the Gaza ceasefire rather than being contained by it

Spain declares a national emergency as wildfires force about 10,000 people from villages around Madrid and nine further serious blazes burn elsewhere, with Ecological Transition Minister Sara Aagesen saying 1,140 square kilometres have burned this year, more than five times the area lost through the first half of 2025; in southwestern France Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reports 40,000 evacuated in Gironde and 23,000 in the Landes, some leaving by boat from the Cap Ferret peninsula, and both governments request EU help, drawing firefighting aircraft from Croatia, Portugal, Italy and Greece and heavy-lift helicopters from Czechia and Slovakia as temperatures are forecast to reach 44C in Almeria

Flooding in India's northeastern Assam state kills at least 50 people and displaces 700,000 after days of heavy monsoon rain overflow the Brahmaputra, submerging nearly 900 villages, cutting power to more than 7,000 homes and forcing close to 300,000 people into government relief camps, with authorities airdropping food and supplies by helicopter to communities cut off by the water

The Trump administration invokes forced-labour provisions of the Trade Act of 1974 to impose new tariffs of 10 percent on the EU, Canada, Mexico and India and 12.5 percent on China, Japan and South Korea; the same day the FAO warns that Strait of Hormuz disruption and war-driven food prices could stall progress against global hunger, which reached 7.8 percent of the world's population, about 645 million people, in 2025, while diesel costs more than 60 percent higher than a year ago are calculated to have cost US farmers an additional 1.4 billion dollars

The Washington Post reports the Trump administration is considering military strikes in Mali against al-Qaeda-affiliated armed groups, which would make Mali the eighth country in which the president has ordered strikes this term, extending the war footing into the Sahel at a moment when the region is already absorbing jihadist pressure, coup aftermaths and a collapsing aid picture

The death toll from the capsizing of the ferry MV Barima in Guyana, which was carrying 133 people when it went down on July 18, reaches 65 confirmed dead as a criminal investigation opens; the captain tested positive for marijuana and officials found the passenger list did not match those aboard, exposing gaps in maritime safety oversight in a country transformed by oil revenue

Pakistan and Iran explore a path back to talks with Washington over the nearly five-month-old war in a push initiated by China, with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni, considered close to the Revolutionary Guard Corps, visiting Islamabad for the second time in ten days and meeting Pakistani leaders and army chief Asim Munir; China's foreign ministry says it 'supports the mediation efforts made by Pakistan and other parties,' though all three Pakistani sources caution that the obstacles remain high

Oil falls for the first time in a week on the reported diplomatic opening, with Brent crude dropping almost 4 percent to settle at 96.78 dollars a barrel after touching 102 the day before; US stocks steady as the S&P 500 adds 3.68 points to 7,411.98 and the Dow rises 235.60 points to 51,947.25, though the Nasdaq falls 161.87 points to 24,975.82 and all three indexes finish the week lower, the Nasdaq down 2.1 percent, with Intel sliding despite beating earnings expectations

Brazil's Supreme Military Court sentences a former Navy commander to 24 years in prison for plotting a coup, a rare instance of institutional accountability reaching the senior officer corps; Argentina wins temporary fiscal breathing room as the CAF development bank approves a 250-million-dollar sovereign risk guarantee within a broader four-billion-dollar refinancing package, and Mexico's Cemex reports second-quarter net profit of 347 million dollars, up 9 percent year on year, raising its 2026 EBITDA growth outlook to 16-17 percent

The Pacific De-Risking Group holds its fifth meeting at the Forum Secretariat, co-chaired by the Governor of the Central Bank of Solomon Islands and the World Bank's Pacific division director, reviewing implementation of the Pacific Correspondent Banking Relationships Roadmap to keep small island economies connected to the global financial system; the region also marks one year since the landmark ICJ climate ruling with a call for action, and a solar energy system funded with New Zealand's foreign ministry is handed over to the government of Niue

Astronomers confirm the first atmosphere ever detected around a rocky planet in another star's habitable zone, finding helium slowly leaking from the super-Earth LHS 1140 b some 48 light-years away in the constellation Cetus; the detection, made with a high-sensitivity spectrograph on the Magellan Clay Telescope in Chile's Atacama Desert and published in Science, suggests the world may have held onto its atmosphere for billions of years and makes it a leading target in the search for habitable conditions beyond the solar system
